text:
mike: quick question for the group: we're finalizing service auth for cross-project calls. idea: central broker mints short-lived signed tokens (JWT-like) that include both service identity and origin project, targets verify locally with cached keys. prefer explicit opt-in for target projects. reactions?

rebecca: sounds good. one nuance: caller identity has two signals: the service principal (who executed) and the origin_project for billing/ownership. both matter for policy and audit.

anita: agree. propose token claim set: `iss`, `sub=svc:<name>`, `orig=proj:NNN`, `perm` (list), `iat`,`exp`, `tid` (token id). keep token compact to reduce header size.

sami: TTL tradeoffs: short (30s) -> safer but broker QPS high. 5-15m sweet spot if signed locally and revocation exists. maybe use TTL tiers by sensitivity.

trent: revocation model? options: 1) introspect (broker call) 2) revocation stream + local cache 3) very short TTL to avoid revocation. we should avoid introspection on path if possible.

mike: what about a hybrid: tokens are signed (no runtime call) and we stream revoked token IDs via Kafka/redis pubsub to edge caches. cache keeps a small bloomfilter for revoked ids for 15m window.

anita: that works. need to define acceptable false-positive/negative characteristics for bloom filters. also ensure `tid` uniqueness and rotation.

rebecca: UX/security: default deny for cross-project calls. target projects opt-in via a whitelist policy. whitelist can be per-role e.g., allow `proj-A` services to call `proj-B:ingest` for `call:ingest` scope.

mike: outline for policy eval pseudo:
```
evaluate(token, resource) {
  if (resource.project != token.orig && !resource.whitelist.includes(token.orig)) return DENY;
  roles = mapPermsToRoles(token.perm);
  return checkRoles(roles, resource.actions);
}
```

trent: fallback if broker down? prefer explicit degraded mode: allow pre-issued long-lived certs but only for limited readonly scopes and only if project has enabled fallback. must be logged and rate-limited.

ops-bot: note: deploy pipelines will need a mint endpoint. we'll add a client lib for ephemeral token requests and retry/backoff patterns.

auth-bot: audit requirement: log `tid`, `sub`, `orig`, `resource`, `policy_decision`, `verifier_key_id` in append-only store for 90 days. tagging for PIIs. :lock:

anita: rotation: broker keypair rotates every 24h with overlap grace so services can cache verification keys for a bit. token `exp` should be <= key overlap window.

rebecca: billing/quota: attribute consumption to `orig` by default. if a service needs to bill the target, require explicit cross:bill scope. avoids surprise chargebacks.

mike: ops note: broker becomes critical infra. SLA target: 99.9% for mint API. but design so normal request path doesn't need broker (signed tokens + cache).

trent: migration: (1) identify long-lived keys used by non-human actors; (2) require migration to broker-issued tokens within 6 months; (3) block non-migrated keys for cross-project calls after 90 days.

anita: I'll draft token schema and TTL tiers. include claim examples and header suggestions.

rebecca: I'll draft whitelist policy spec and admin UX (one-click approve + audit email on first use).

mike: i'll own broker availability/caching architecture doc + revocation streaming design.

mike: next steps: create RFC with schema + revocation strategy + whitelist + migration timeline. @anita @rebecca please volunteer to review, then we'll post for wider eng review.

rebecca: +1. thanks everyone. I'll open an issue and link the RFC draft by EOD. :memo:
